did.abstract: In 1955, the University of Michigan suspended three professors (H. Chandler Davis, Mark Nickerson and Clement Markert) for their refusal to give testimony before a U.S. House Committee on Un-American Activities. In 1990, the Academic Freedom Lecture Fund (AFLF) was established to honor those professors. From 1991-2018, AFLF organized the annual Davis, Markert, Nickerson Lecture on Academic and Intellectual Freedom. This collection consists of the administrative records of the AFLF, as well as material related to the planning and execution of the lectures and symposia, including recordings and transcriptions.

acqinfo.p: Donated by the Academic Freedom Lecture Fund (Donor no. 8703) in 2001, 2002, 2003, 2006, 2022, 2023, and 2024.

bioghist.p: In 1955, during the height of the McCarthy era, the University of Michigan suspended professors H. Chandler Davis, Clement Markert, and Mark Nickerson for their refusal to give testimony before a U.S. House Committee on Un-American Activities panel. Davis and Nickerson (a tenured professor) were terminated. Markert was later reinstated. The national American Association of University Professors (AAUP) censured the university for its treatment of these professors in 1957. After a new Regents' Bylaw (5.09) was adopted, censure was removed in 1958.

In 1988, emeritus professor Wilbert J. McKeachie published an article, "Reminiscences of the 1950's," in the University of Michigan AAUP Chapter Newsletter that detailed the treatment of Davis, Markert and Nickerson at Michigan during the 1950s. David Hollinger, a history professor, also wrote an account of those events for the 1988 Centennial Celebration Bulletin of the Horace H. Rackham School of Graduate Studies. Those accounts prompted student Adam Kulakow to prepare a video documentary on the Davis, Markert, Nickerson cases for his undergraduate honors dissertation. Kulakow's documentary Keeping in Mind - The McCarthy Era at the University of Michigan, was shown publicly on April 9, 1989, to a large audience that included the three professors.

Following the presentation of Keeping in Mind, a member of the audience suggested that the university be asked to make amends for its treatment of the three professors in 1955. The University of Michigan Chapter of the AAUP pursued the matter, hoping to encourage the Regents to take appropriate action. A proposal was sent to the Senate Advisory Committee on University Affairs (SACUA) in October 1989. The proposal was endorsed in February 1990 by the Senate Assembly. When the Regents did not take action, the Senate Assembly passed a resolution in November 1990 that deeply regretted "the failure of the University Community to protect the values of intellectual freedom" in 1955. The resolution also established the annual University of Michigan Senate's Davis, Markert, Nickerson Lecture on Academic and Intellectual Freedom. The first lecture was given on February 18, 1991. The three professors were present and participated in a panel discussion after the lecture.

The Senate Assembly established an Academic Freedom Lecture Fund (AFLF) to support public lectures on academic freedom wherever they might be given. AFLF was subsequently established as an independent non-profit organization in 1991.
In 2000, the University of Michigan Press published Unfettered Expression: Freedom in American Intellectual Life. The book, edited by Peggie J. Hollingsworth, contains essays originally given as lectures in the annual Davis, Markert, Nickerson Lecture on Academic and Intellectual Freedom series at the University of Michigan from 1991 to 1999.

The AFLF remained the primary organizer of the Davis, Markert, Nickerson lectures until 2018, when the SACUA moved to take over the role. Additional changes within SACUA and the Faculty Senate Office, as well as the determination by U-M General Counsel that the AFLF was to be considered outside of the University due to its 501(c)(3) status, complicated the AFLF's relationship with these organizations and ultimately made collaboration infeasible.
The AFLF Board moved to dissolve the fund in 2022, however the Davis, Markert, Nickerson lecture has continued under the U-M Faculty Senate Office.

scopecontent.p: This collection documents the activities of the Academic Freedom Lecture Fund (AFLF), and is arranged into two series: (1) Administrative records, and (2) the Davis, Markert, Nickerson Lectures on Academic and Intellectual Freedom. The Administrative records series includes files which document the internal activities of the AFLF, including Board of Directors meetings and correspondence, financial records, general correspondence, and a visiting professorship position proposed by the AFLF. Also included are files related to the organizational history of the AFLF, including contextual records regarding the establishment and dissolution of the fund as well as dedicated files for professors Chandler Davis, Clement Markert, and Mark Nickerson.

The Davis, Markert, Nickerson Lectures on Academic and Intellectual Freedom series includes records related to the planning and execution of this lecture series. This series includes recordings and transcriptions of lectures and speaker interviews, as well as versions of Adam Kulakow's documentary Keeping in Mind. The speaker files subseries includes material related to the planning and booking of speakers, including correspondence, programs, itineraries, and more. The publicity series comprises records related to the promotion of the lecture series to the general public. Also included are materials related to the planning and execution of the larger tenth-anniversary symposium in 2000.

relatedmaterial.p: The Bentley Historical Library houses the following related collections: Adam Kulakow papers, Peggie J. Hollingsworth papers, American Association of University Professors, University of Michigan Chapter, records, and Mark Nickerson sound recording collection.

processinfo.p: In August 2026, archivist Evan Brandon significantly revised the finding aid, following the processing of accessions acquired from 2022-2024. The existing collection contents were absorbed into the Lecture and interview transcriptions and recordings subseries of the Davis, Markert, Nickerson Lectures series.

In preparing digital material for long-term preservation and access, the Bentley Historical Library adheres to professional best practices and standards to ensure that content will retain its authenticity and integrity. For more information on procedures for the ingest and processing of digital materials, please see Bentley Historical Library Digital Processing Note. scopecontent.p: This series contains records relating to the organizational context, function, and activities of the AFLF. Subseries include: Organizational history, Board of Directors meeting minutes and correspondence, Financial records, Visiting professorship, and General correspondence.

This sub-series consists of material that provides context for the formation and eventual dissolution of the AFLF. Included are files relating to Chandler Davis, Clement Markert, and Mark Nickerson and their reconciliation with the University of Michigan, as well as files of significant members of the Board of Directors throughout the AFLF's lifespan. Also included are materials related to the screening and distribution of Adam E. Kulakow's documentary, Keeping in Mind.
